_meta.semantics: covers_syllabus_refs is an index of the objectives a stage is principally associated with; coverage is claimed only through _syllabus_items + covers_items, and only as far as coverage_check.py confirms.

_items_source.document: Pearson Edexcel Level 3 Advanced GCE in Politics (9PL0) specification, Issue 4: Component 1 (UK Politics and Core Political Ideas), Component 2 (UK Government and Non-core Political Ideas, Feminism option) and Component 3A (Comparative Politics: Government and Politics of the USA)
_items_source.version: Issue 4 (May 2026), the current specification (first teaching September 2017, unchanged since), linked from qualifications.pearson.com and itemised 2026-09-27
_items_source.numbering: Edexcel numbers the content areas and sub-points (e.g. 1.1-1.4 for Democracy and participation; 3.3.1-3.3.2 for the Prime Minister and Cabinet) but leaves the thinkers, ideology tensions and much comparative content as unnumbered bullets. This course codes UK Politics by topic-prefix and sub-point (DP1.1-1.4 Democracy and participation, PP2.1-2.4 Political parties, ES3.1-3.3 Electoral systems, VB4.1-4.2 Voting behaviour and the media); Core Political Ideas by ideology and unnumbered content area (CON/LIB/SOC .1 core ideas, .2 tensions, .3 thinkers); UK Government the same way as UK Politics (GOV1.1-1.4 the constitution, GOV2.1-2.4 Parliament, GOV3.1-3.3 Prime Minister and executive, GOV4.1-4.4 relations between branches); the Feminism option and the four unselected non-core ideas (Anarchism, Ecologism, Multiculturalism, Nationalism) the same way as the core ideas (FEM/ANA/ECO/MC/NAT .1-.3); and Component 3A USA content by topic-prefix and Edexcel's own sub-numbering where it exists (USC1.1-1.4 US Constitution and federalism, CONG2.1-2.3 US Congress structure/functions/interpretations, PRES3.1-3.4 US presidency, SCOTUS4.1-4.6 US Supreme Court and civil rights, USDEM5.1-5.4 US democracy and participation, COMP6.1-6.5+UK/US pairings for comparative theories).
